title: Earpod Tree: Old Guanacaste Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: A wide, spreading tree whose coiled seed pods look like ears. Fort Canning's is 5.94 m round, Waialua's is 6.95 m, and Flamingo Gardens holds Florida's champion.
intro: The earpod tree, Enterolobium cyclocarpum, comes from the tropical dry forests of Central America and takes its name from its dark, coiled seed pods, which curl into the shape of a human ear. In Costa Rica, where it is the national tree, it is called guanacaste. Planted in other warm countries, it grows wide rather than tall. Flamingo Gardens in Davie, Florida, holds the state's champion, over six metres round. The one at Fort Canning in Singapore has been on the heritage register since 2001, at 5.94 metres of girth and 17.9 metres tall. On Oahu the Waialua library car park shades a 6.95 metre trunk, said to date from 1902. On Kauai a tree outside a Koloa funeral home is filed as an earpod while the mayor called it a monkeypod, and the pods would settle it.
